proof_summary: Quadratic reciprocity makes \(5\) a square modulo \(p\); taking a square root \(x\) and setting \(n=x-1\) gives \(3\le n<p\) and \(n^2+2n-4=kp\). Continuant identities, supplemented by parity in the even-cofactor cases, show \(k\mid S(n,3)\), whereas \(p\mid S(n,3)\) would propagate through the recurrence to \(p\mid S(n,n)=4\); hence the fraction is \(p/Q\) with \(p\nmid Q\), so its reduced numerator is exactly \(p\).
